body.x: ITWell (President Won-Sik Kim, www.itwell.co.kr) exhibited UBITA3500/4300, an international security standard certified wireless payment device, and XPDA-T5.7/XPDA-T8/XPDA-T10.1 for android phones and tablets, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

UBITA3500 is a wireless payment device for industrial use that has been PCI-PED 4.0 and EMV L1 & L2 certified to meet the international security standard. This all-in-one product uses TI Cortex A81G processor, Window CE 6.0 and Android 4.2 OS and supports 512MB RAM and 1GB NAND Flash. It can take 1G to 4G memory flash and works with many connection methods like WLAN, RFiD, and BT.

UBITA4300 is another wireless payment device for industrial use that also has been PCI-PED 4.0 and EMV L1 & L2 certified. It supports iMX6 Quad Core, 1.2GHz CPU, 1G DDR RAM, and 4GB NAND Flash and utilizes Android 4.2 OS.

XPDA-T5.7/XPDA-T8/XPDA-T10.1 were also presented at the tradeshow. These products support payment and automatic data collection systems for Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 with both 5.7" and 8" display and Galaxy Tab 10.1, to provide smart options in the industrial transaction market. After installing the payment application, the credit card-reading sleeve should be attached to the smartphone or the tablet.

The company spokesperson said, "Unlike the limited functions of the existing products, our product can be used for all-purposes and is durable and secure. We hope to expand our client base beyond North America and reach South America and Europe."

ITWell is a wire/wireless POS specialty company established in 1998. It pursued the foreign markets starting in 2004 and is currently distributing its products to North America, Europe, Asia, Middle East, and Africa. It is supplying 60% of the products to a North American airline.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
